title: Fever’s Caitlin Clark to miss second game of season due to back injury
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark will not play in Saturday’s home game against the Los Angeles Sparks due to a back injury, coach Stephanie White announced at practice Friday. This will mark the second time this season Clark misses a game because of the issue.

After their game versus the Sparks, the Fever have seven days before their next game, at the Las Vegas Aces on July 5. White said she did not have an indication of how long Clark would be out.

Clark exited Wednesday’s loss to the Phoenix Mercury in the third quarter after aggravating her back injury. The two-time All-Star has been managing back issues all season, even leaving the season opener multiple times to get her “back adjusted,” per Clark.

The Fever likely will turn to veteran Tyasha Harris and rookie Raven Johnson to handle point guard duties while Clark is sidelined. Kelsey Mitchell, the Fever’s starting shooting guard, said she’d also be ready to take on more ballhandling and play-making responsibilities in Clark’s absence.

Clark got tangled up with Mercury veteran Alyssa Thomas in Wednesday’s contest. White said after the game, “I’m not sure if it had any impact on (Clark’s) health,” but she blasted the referees for missing the second-quarter incident. Clark lost her balance while dribbling down the lane, and when she fell to the ground, Thomas dove on the floor to try to get the ball away from Clark. Thomas, however, appeared to use a closed right fist to push down on Clark’s neck during the scrum.

The incident was initially a no-call, but Thursday, the WNBA upgraded the play to a flagrant 2 penalty and Thomas was given a one-game suspension for “recklessly making contact with her fist to the throat area” of Clark, the league said in a statement. Thomas will serve her suspension, the first in her 13-year career, when the Mercury face the Toronto Tempo on the road Saturday.

White, who coached Thomas for two seasons with the Connecticut Sun, said after the game that Thomas’ action was “crazy” and “dangerous.” White added that she thought the Mercury got away with “two cheap shots” on Clark, the other being when Mercury forward Valériane Ayayi fouled Clark on a 3-pointer in the second quarter by not giving her enough space to land safely. Clark took an awkward fall on the play and rubbed her back as she stood up, though it’s unclear if that contributed to her back injury.

Clark missed her first game of the season, a 90-73 home win over the Portland Fire on May 20, due to a sore back. She had been listed on the injury report as probable due to her back in the 13 games since.

Clark said earlier this season that she isn’t sure when her back issues began. She’s been wearing a heating pad on her back when she’s on the bench this season, which she did not do in her first two years.

“I don’t think it necessarily started at a certain point,” Clark said in May. “I think it’s just been over the course of the last year when I’ve kind of been understanding my body more. … Still working through that, but I don’t think it’s anything of concern.”

Clark appeared in just 13 games last year due to various injuries. She’s already appeared in 17 games this season, averaging 21.2 points, 8.2 assists and 4.0 rebounds.
